arxiv-1806-07172.title: Surrogate Outcomes and Transportability
arxiv-1806-07172.creator: S. Tikka, J. Karvanen
arxiv-1806-07172.description: Abstract Identification of causal effects is one of the most fundamental tasks of causal inference. We consider an identifiability problem where some experimental and observational data are available but neither data alone is sufficient for the identification of the causal effect of interest. Instead of the outcome of interest, surrogate outcomes are measured in the experiments.

arxiv-2107-10102.title: Instances of small size with no weakly stable matching for three-sided problem with complete cyclic preferences
arxiv-2107-10102.creator: Lerner E.Yu
arxiv-2107-10102.description: Abstract Given n n men, n n women, and n n dogs, we assume that each man has a complete preference list of women, while each woman does a complete preference list of dogs, and each dog does a complete preference list of men. We study the so-called 3D-CYC problem, i.e., a three-dimensional problem with cyclic preferences.

arxiv-2110-02879.title: Compositional Q-learning for electrolyte repletion with imbalanced patient sub-populations
arxiv-2110-02879.creator: Aishwarya Mandyam, Andrew Jones, Jiayu Yao, Krzysztof Laudanski, Barbara E. Engelhardt
arxiv-2110-02879.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective framework for solving sequential decision-making tasks. However, applying RL methods in medical care settings is challenging in part due to heterogeneity in treatment response among patients. Some patients can be treated with standard protocols whereas others, such as those with chronic diseases, need personalized treatment planning.

arxiv-2310-00646.title: Source Attribution for Large Language Model-Generated Data
arxiv-2310-00646.creator: Jingtan Wang*, Xinyang Lu*, Zitong Zhao*, Chuan-Sheng Foo
arxiv-2310-00646.description: Abstract The impressive performances of large language models (LLMs) and their immense potential for commercialization have given rise to serious concerns over the intellectual property (IP) of their training data. In particular, the synthetic texts generated by LLMs may infringe the IP of the data being used to train the LLMs.

arxiv-2405-08351.title: KG-EmpiRE: A Community-Maintainable Knowledge Graph for a Sustainable Literature Review on the State and Evolution of Empirical Research in Requirements Engineering
arxiv-2405-08351.creator: Oliver Karras 1
arxiv-2405-08351.description: Abstract In the last two decades, several researchers provided snapshots of the “current” state and evolution of empirical research in requirements engineering (RE) through literature reviews. However, these literature reviews were not sustainable, as none built on or updated previous works due to the unavailability of the extracted and analyzed data.

arxiv-2411-05056.title: Seeing is Deceiving: Exploitation of Visual Pathways in Multi-Modal Language Models
arxiv-2411-05056.creator: Pete Janowczyk # , Linda Laurier + , Ave Giulietta † , Arlo Octavia ‡ , Meade Cleti *, §
arxiv-2411-05056.description: Abstract Multi-Modal Language Models (MLLMs) have transformed artificial intelligence by combining visual and text data, making applications like image captioning, visual question answering, and multi-modal content creation possible. This ability to understand and work with complex information has made MLLMs useful in areas such as healthcare, autonomous systems, and digital content.

pmc-12735159.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Pathological Stage, Tumor Characteristics and Surgical Outcomes of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Retrospective Analysis
pmc-12735159.creator: Samer Omari, Murad AbdelRaziq, Kutaiba Alkeesh, Alaa Muhana, Imad Abu El-Naaj, Yasmin Ghantous, Luca Aquilanti, Giorgio Rappelli
pmc-12735159.description: Background and Objectives: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) requires early diagnosis for favorable outcomes, but global healthcare disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic severely affected cancer care delivery. This study aimed to investigate the pandemic’s influence on OSCC pathological staging and disease-related characteristics at a single medical center.

pmc-13129373.title: Predictors of device-related adverse events in patients with intra-aortic ballon pump or microaxial flow pump for cardiogenic shock
pmc-13129373.creator: Zachary Provenzano, Zachary Patel, Cecil Jnawali, Roxanne Mittelstaedt, Meg Ospina, Stephanie Samani, Jacob Peller, Charlotte Marchell, Kelly Ohlrich, Brady Gunn, Michael Varrone, Kaylen Dodson, Lindsey Bull, Jennifer Hajj, Mathew J Gregoski, Ryan J Tedford, Walker Blanding, Jeffery McMurray, Lucas
pmc-13129373.description: Device-related adverse events (DRAEs) are common with intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) and microaxial flow pump (mAFP) in cardiogenic shock (CS), yet predictors of DRAEs are underrecognized. We performed a single-center, retrospective review of consecutive adults from 8/2021 to 8/2024 with CS and IABP or mAFP. Events were adjudicated as device-related if occurring during IABP/mAFP support or <72 hours of removal.

pmc-13576272.title: A bispecific-aptamer TSHR-CD80-1 treats thyroid eye disease by inhibiting CD8+ T cell-fibroblast interactions
pmc-13576272.creator: Jiamin Cao, Zhaochangci Chen, Lemeng Feng, Bingyu Xie, Yao Tan, Wei Xiong, Feng Zhang
pmc-13576272.description: Thyroid eye disease (TED), an autoimmune disorder, involves critical interactions among immune cells that drive disease progression. However, the underlying mechanisms and their therapeutic potential remain unclear. This study profiled leukocyte composition in the peripheral blood of TED patients, revealing an elevated proportion of CD8+ T cells and distinct T-cell receptor (TCR) characteristics.
